title: geogen save v1
description: A saved game: what `geogen.rules.Machine.save` returns and what the Godot runtime writes (`--save`, API `state.save`). Semantics: docs/rules.md, 'Saving'. World and actor state are separate sections, each a flat {key: value}: a key names its owner, so nothing is nested. Only values that differ from their declared defaults are stored; a key that is absent has its default. Bindings are never saved. A single-player game writes every section to one file; a server can keep the actor sections apart.

package.description: The package that was loaded when it was saved (written by the runtime).

now.description: Seconds the rules program has run: what timers' `at` is measured on.

clock.description: The world clock the conditions read.

world.description: Shared state. '<thing id>#<name>' is instance state: a declared variable of one placed instance, or an interaction ('<thing id>#<interaction>' is the state it is in or heading to, '<thing id>#<interaction>_locked' its lock). 'world:<package>.<name>' is a world variable. 'once:<rule>' and 'watch:<rule>' are the latches of rules that aren't per actor. An export without stable IDs keys its interactions '<node name>/<interaction>'.

actors.description: Per actor ('player', or an NPC's stable ID) its 'actor:<package>.<name>' values and the latches of per-actor rules.

actor_info.description: What the program knows of each actor besides its state. Optional: actors a save doesn't describe stay as the host knows them.

room.description: The room it is in ('' for none): `actor.room`.

timers.description: What is still to happen, in firing order (`at`, then `seq`).

npcs.description: NPCs by stable ID, written by runtimes that run them: their needs, whether they are away, how long ago they last used each option (seconds), and where they are: on an affordance ('seat', its id: loading puts them back on it) or at 'position' facing 'yaw' degrees. What they were otherwise doing isn't kept: they decide again. Machine.load ignores it.

characters.description: Named people (NPCs placed from kind: character files) by actor ID ('character:<name>'), as last seen in whichever scene that was: their needs. Placed in another scene they carry on from these; where they are stays per placement in 'npcs'. Machine.load ignores it.

flows.description: Spawned items (geogen/flows.py), written by runtimes that run them: the items in the world (on a track by its stable ID and distance 's', or a physics item's pose) and how far each source (its wave phase and timers, its pick) and effector (its cooldown) had got. Counts are rules state in 'world'. Loading takes the items in the world away and brings these back.

bodies.description: Physics props (extras.geogen.physics) that are live, by stable ID: where they are. Written by runtimes that simulate them; a prop it doesn't name is where its spawn interaction puts it.

packages.description: Written by a runtime: every other package visited this session, by name, as it was left (a save of its own, without `packages` or `carried`). Loading resumes each when its scene loads; one made in another scene loads that scene's part from here.

carried.description: Written by a runtime: content packages' values (docs/rules.md 'Content packages'), whatever scene is loaded, as {world: {key: value}, actors: {actor: {key: value}}}.

at.description: When it fires, on `now`'s scale (a wait in seconds).

clock.description: Instead of `at`, for a wait in clock time: the clock minute it fires at (day * 1440 + minutes into the day).

seq.description: The order it was scheduled in: ties go to the lower.

kind.description: rule: a rule's `after` ran out, its effects are due. arrive: an interaction reaches the state it is heading to. dwell: a state's own `after` ran out, it moves on to its `then`. every: a periodic rule's period is up: it runs if its condition holds, and the next period starts from this due time.

rule.description: kind rule, every: the rule's id.

state.description: kind arrive, dwell: the state it arrives at or dwells in.

from.description: kind arrive, optional: the state it set out from, so a runtime whose things really move can put one back part of the way (`at` is when it gets there). Evaluators ignore it.

actor.description: The actor behind it ('' or null: nobody).

data.description: kind rule, optional: the data of the event that fired the rule, for a rule that reads it (event.<field>).
